title: Completion comparison for constant supported etale cohomology
statement:
Let $A$ be an excellent Noetherian henselian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $\ell$ be prime and invertible in $A$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Put $\widehat A=\varprojlim_rA/\mathfrak m^r$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\widehat S=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, and let $s,\widehat s$ be their closed points [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every $q,m\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical pullback is an isomorphism
$$H^q_s(S,\Lambda(m))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q_{\widehat s}(\widehat S,\Lambda(m)).$$
Supported cohomology is the ordinary etale derived closed-support functor [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections], and the twists are the signed roots-of-unity twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-sheaf]. No regularity or finite-type-over-a-field assumption is made.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.3, printed p. 279, application of formal base change to the constant invertible finite coefficients; the cited original is Fujiwara 1995, Corollary 6.6.4

proof.text: Write $f:\widehat S\to S$ for the completion morphism and $k=A/\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $\widehat A$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], it is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$, and the induced map $k\to\widehat A/\mathfrak m\widehat A$ is an isomorphism. The quotient maps define closed immersions $i:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow S$ and $\widehat i:\widehat s\hookrightarrow\widehat S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion]. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $\widehat S\times_Ss$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A\otimes_A k)=\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A/\mathfrak m\widehat A)=\widehat s$. The tensor-to-quotient map sends $b\otimes\bar a$ to $b f^\sharp(a)$ modulo $\mathfrak m\widehat A$, with inverse $\bar b\mapsto b\otimes1$; these are well-defined mutually inverse maps. Thus the closed square is cartesian and its lower-dimensional projection $\rho:\widehat s\to s$ is the residue-field isomorphism. Both $S$ and $\widehat S$ are Noetherian schemes, and $\ell$ remains invertible on $\widehat S$ because its inverse in $A$ maps to an inverse in $\widehat A$.

proof.text: Excellence implies the G-ring property by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Apply [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] at the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Since all elements outside $\mathfrak m$ are already units, $A_{\mathfrak m}=A$, and its local completion is precisely $\widehat A$. Consequently $A\to\widehat A$ is flat, and each fibre algebra $B_{\mathfrak p}=\widehat A\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], $f$ is flat as a scheme morphism. For every finite field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] makes $K\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}B_{\mathfrak p}$ a regular Noetherian ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], its spectrum is the corresponding base change of the fibre of $f$, hence is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. This verifies exactly the flatness and geometrically regular fibres required for regular base change. No regularity of $A$ itself is asserted.

proof.text: For either closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ in Step 1, with open complement $j$, put $P_ZF=\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$ and $i^!_0F=i^*P_ZF$. The statement of [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction] gives $P_ZF\cong i_*i^!_0F$, the adjunction $i_*\dashv i^!_0$, and exactness of $i_*$ on abelian sheaves. These assertions also hold on sheaves of constant $\Lambda$-modules: all maps are natural for each scalar endomorphism of $F$, so the displayed isomorphism is $\Lambda$-linear, and an adjoint transpose is $\Lambda$-linear exactly when the original map is (apply naturality to multiplication by each $\lambda\in\Lambda$). Exactness follows by the exact faithful forgetful functor of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. If $I$ is injective and $N\hookrightarrow N'$ is a module-sheaf monomorphism on $Z$, exactness of $i_*$ and injectivity of $I$ make $\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*N',I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*N,I)$ surjective. The adjunction identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N',i^!_0I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,i^!_0I)$. Thus $i^!_0I$ is injective by the definition of injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

proof.text: Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Choose a bounded-below injective module-sheaf representative $I$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], $i^!K$ is represented by $i^!_0I$. Step 3 says its terms are injective on $Z$, so that same result computes $R\Gamma(Z,i^!K)$ by $\Gamma(Z,i^!_0I)$. The isomorphism $P_ZI\cong i_*i^!_0I$ identifies this complex termwise with $\Gamma(X,P_ZI)=\ker(\Gamma(X,I)\to\Gamma(X\setminus Z,j^*I))$. By [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections] this last complex computes $R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$. We obtain the natural identification $R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\cong R\Gamma(Z,i^!K)$, normalized by the actual inclusion of the kernel into $\Gamma(X,I)$. Naturality follows termwise from the natural kernel isomorphism; comparison maps and homotopies between injective representatives retain that equality.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] to the cartesian closed square of Step 1, the regular morphism $f$ of Step 2, and $K=\Lambda_S(m)[0]$. Its Noetherian and invertible-$\ell$ assumptions hold by Step 1, and a sheaf in degree zero is bounded below. It yields the canonical isomorphism $\beta_K:\rho^*i^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat i^!f^*K$. Apply [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] with coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and modulus $\ell^n$ to identify $f^*\Lambda_S(m)$ canonically with $\Lambda_{\widehat S}(m)$ for every signed integer $m$. In particular no choice of a root of unity or trivialization of the twist enters. The regular-supported comparison is specified by the closed counits and localization triangles, so this is the canonical supported comparison, with its stated normalization.

proof.text:
Under the identifications of Step 4, the supported pullback is the composite
$$R\Gamma(s,i^!K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(\widehat s,\rho^*i^!K)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(\widehat s,\beta_K)}R\Gamma(\widehat s,\widehat i^!f^*K).$$
Here is a representative check of this assertion, rather than only an abstract isomorphism of the groups. Take an injective representative $K\to I$ on $S$, an injective resolution $f^*K\to J$ on $\widehat S$, and a comparison chain map $f^*I\to J$ extending it; bounded-below K-injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] supplies such a representative in the homotopy category. The sheaf pullback sends $P_sI$ into $P_{\widehat s}f^*I$, since a section whose restriction to the open complement is zero still restricts to zero after base change. Applying $f^*I\to J$ gives the chain map on supported kernels. Through Step 3 it is the map $\rho^*i^!_0I\to\widehat i^!_0J$ whose closed counit composite is the pulled-back supported inclusion. The bounded-below derived adjunction [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction], applied to the exact module-sheaf adjunction $\widehat i_*\dashv\widehat i^!_0$ of Step 3 (enough injectives by Step 4), gives $\widehat i_*\dashv\widehat i^!$ on $D^+$; by its counit formula the derived counit at the injective complex $J$ is the class of the termwise counit $\widehat i_*\widehat i^!_0J\cong P_{\widehat s}J\subset J$. By the adjunction bijection, a map into $\widehat i^!f^*K$ is determined by its composite with this counit. The canonical-counit specification in [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] gives $\beta_K$ the same composite, the pullback of the counit of $K$; hence the derived class of the chain map is $\beta_K$. Taking sections and using Step 4 therefore gives exactly the displayed composite for the pullback defined by restriction of supported sections. A different comparison chain map gives a homotopic map, so the check is independent of these representatives.

proof.text: Since $\rho:\widehat s\to s$ is the isomorphism of Step 1, pulling a sheaf back along $\rho$ just transports it to the isomorphic etale site; its global sections and injective resolutions are transported by inverse equivalences. Thus the first arrow in Step 6 is an isomorphism. The second is an isomorphism because $\beta_K$ is one. Applying cohomology in degree $q$ to that composite and using the identification $f^*K=\Lambda_{\widehat S}(m)$ of Step 5 proves the required canonical isomorphism $H^q_s(S,\Lambda(m))\to H^q_{\widehat s}(\widehat S,\Lambda(m))$. This applies to every integer $q$; for $q<0$ both groups vanish since they are derived from a sheaf in degree zero by a left exact functor. The argument needs no finite type hypothesis on $f$, no regularity hypothesis on $S$, and no replacement of $s$ by a geometric point.
